title: A ceiling is a maximum, not a target
text: The ceiling is the most refugees the President authorizes for the fiscal year ("the admission of up to N refugees"). Admissions below it are not a shortfall against a quota, and admissions above it are not allowed. It covers refugees resettled from abroad only: asylum seekers (who apply from inside the U.S. or at the border), Temporary Protected Status holders and parolees are different statuses and are not counted here.

title: FY1980 has no ceiling here
text: The Refugee Act of 1980 (signed March 17, 1980) created the annual consultation and Presidential Determination under INA section 207. FY1980 was a transition year; no determination text or government compilation for its ceiling was located, so the FY1980 ceiling is missing, not estimated. FY1980 admissions are shown.

title: State Department and DHS counts differ slightly
text: The State Department's WRAPS counts (used here) differ from DHS's Yearbook of Immigration Statistics refugee arrivals, which come from DHS records and are rounded to tens before FY2013 (e.g. FY1992: 132,531 vs. 115,550). DHS figures are a cross-check only (refugee_report.json) and are never mixed in.

title: Ceilings FY1981–FY1986 and FY1990 come from CRS, not the determination text
text: No machine-readable text of the FY1981–FY1986 and FY1990 Presidential Determinations was located (the 1980s Federal Register is only available as whole-issue scans), so those years' final ceilings come from CRS Report R47399, Table A-1, which compiles the final ceiling from the determinations and emergency determinations. Every year where both are available agrees with the determinations (checked at build time). The initial ceiling and any mid-year revision of those years are not known here.

title: Asylee adjustment numbers are separate
text: Determinations through FY2016 also make 5,000–10,000 numbers available for asylees to adjust to permanent residence. Those numbers are not part of the refugee ceiling and are not stored.

title: Privately funded admissions (FY1987–FY1995)
text: From FY1987 to FY1995 part of each ceiling was reserved for privately funded admissions (the Private Sector Initiative, PSI), usable for any region if private sponsors paid the costs. They count toward the ceiling; the State Department's table shows their admissions in a separate PSI column (FY1988–FY1993).

title: FY1987 reserve was privately funded
text: PD 87-1's 4,000-number unallocated reserve could be used only with private-sector funding.

title: Amerasian immigrants are inside the East Asia numbers
text: From FY1988 the ceilings and the East Asia allocation include Amerasian immigrants (children of U.S. servicemen in Vietnam and their families) admitted with refugee resettlement assistance, and the State Department's Asia column marks FY1989–FY2019 "Includes Amerasian Immigrants".

title: FY1989 was raised during the year
text: PD 89-2 set 94,000; CRS Report R47399 gives the final FY1989 ceiling as 116,500. The emergency determination(s) that raised it were not located, so the revision's date and allocation are unknown here.

title: FY1999 raised for Kosovo
text: PD 99-33 (Aug 12, 1999) found an unforeseen refugee emergency in Europe and raised the FY1999 ceiling from 78,000 to 91,000 for Kosovar refugees. The State Department's table shows Kosovo admissions as their own column (14,161 in FY1999).

title: Country of chargeability is not always the country fled
text: The State Department's country rows are by country of chargeability, and its regions by the nationality of the principal applicant. A refugee is usually counted under nationality, which can differ from the country they fled or were processed in (e.g. Burmese refugees processed in Malaysia or Thailand count under Burma).

title: Regional allocations are reallocated during the year
text: The determination's regional numbers are a starting allocation: unallocated reserves are assigned and unused numbers moved between regions during the year (after notifying Congress). The State Department's year-end regional ceilings (FY2001 on) show the result and often differ from the determination (FY2013 Africa: 12,000 in PD 2012-17, 15,950 at year end); the worldwide ceiling matches the determination every year.

title: FY2017: 110,000 ceiling, 50,000 cap by executive order
text: PD 2016-13 set 110,000. Executive Orders 13769 (Jan 27, 2017) and 13780 (Mar 6, 2017) each proclaimed that entry of more than 50,000 refugees in FY2017 would be detrimental and suspended entries above that number, and suspended the program for 120 days. The ceiling of record stays 110,000 (the State Department's sheet prints 110,000); 53,716 were admitted.

title: Some later arrivals count toward the FY2018 ceiling
text: Under the settlement in Doe et al. v. Trump et al., No. 17-0178 (W.D. Wash.), certain refugee applicants who arrive in FY2020 and later fiscal years are counted toward the FY2018 ceiling (State Department note). The admissions shown are by year of arrival, as the State Department tables them. The State Department's FY2018 total has also risen since earlier vintages (CRS, as of Nov 2022: 22,615; current: 22,676).

title: FY2020 and early FY2021 were allocated by category, not region
text: PD 2020-04 and PD 2021-02 divided the ceiling among kinds of refugees (religious persecution and Lautenberg/Specter categories, Iraqis under the Refugee Crisis in Iraq Act, Northern Triangle nationals, others) rather than regions; PD 2021-02 also barred refugees from Somalia, Syria and Yemen outside narrow exceptions. PD 2021-05 (Apr 16, 2021) returned to regional allocations.

title: The pandemic depressed FY2020–FY2021 admissions on its own
text: Refugee travel was largely halted in spring 2020 by the COVID-19 pandemic. PD 2021-02 says its 15,000 ceiling incorporates more than 6,000 unused FY2020 places that might have been used if not for the pandemic. Low admissions in these years are not only a policy choice.

title: FY2024–FY2025 regional allocations are ranges
text: PD 2023-13 and PD 2024-13 allocate a range per region (e.g. Africa 30,000–50,000), with the total capped at 125,000.

title: Refugee entry suspended from Jan 27, 2025
text: Executive Order 14163 (Jan 20, 2025) suspended entry of refugees under USRAP from 12:01 a.m. Jan 27, 2025, except case-by-case admissions the Secretaries of State and Homeland Security jointly find in the national interest. FY2025's 125,000 ceiling was set by the previous administration; 37,596 of FY2025's 38,102 admissions arrived October–January. The FY2026 and FY2027 determinations are made subject to EO 14163 and to the entry restrictions of Proclamations 10949/10998.

title: FY2026 admissions are the first year-end report
text: FY2026 ended Sept 30, 2026; the State Department's report is as of that date (data run Oct 4). Earlier years have shifted slightly in later vintages, so FY2026 is preliminary.

title: FY2026–FY2027 are allocated to a group, not regions
text: PD 2025-13 allocates FY2026 admissions "primarily" to Afrikaners from South Africa under Executive Order 14204 and other victims of illegal or unjust discrimination; PD 2026-14 (May 21, 2026) raised the ceiling from 7,500 to 17,500 with the additional admissions allocated to Afrikaners; PD 2026-24 sets FY2027 at 17,500, "primarily" Afrikaners. No numeric allocation by region exists for these years.
